claim_type_rationale: Single console-ranking master defines the 5-partition universe (top 5 consoles by lifetime units sold per `List of best-selling game consoles`); 5 dedicated per-console best-seller list pages supply the top-3 ranked titles + Units Sold + Release Year cells per partition. The only curator-chosen input is N=5 (the partition-count threshold), which is a deterministic numeric cut on the master's units-sold ranking. The within-partition K=3 is the source's own top-3 ranking from each per-console page. Same source-pattern as zodiac-stars (1 Zodiac master + 12 per-constellation list pages = source_count 13 with claim_type source_defined). Distinct from `partially_supplemented` (no rebuilding of any subset; both universe + per-partition ranking are from source). The deterministic-universe-rule preference is satisfied: SQL-WHERE = `console_rank_by_lifetime_units_sold <= 5 AND title_rank_within_console <= 3`.

collection_summary.approach: Pre-curation design pass (cycle-0 source exploration + audit-cycle-1 design review APPROVE-WITH-AMENDMENTS) produced a source-faithful instance. PIVOT from `top_5_oldest_universities_per_continent` after cycle-0 hit a WebFetch tool truncation on that master article — half the per-continent sub-sections (Latin America+Caribbean, North America, Oceania, partial Asia) were unreachable, making source-faithful staging infeasible. Pivot rationale + universities prior cycle-1 design review are documented in the comments.json trail for that staged-but-not-locked instance. The video-games candidate uses bounded per-console list pages which fetched reliably across all 5 partitions during cycle-0 (Nintendo Switch test fetch confirmed Mario Kart 8 Deluxe 71.08M / Animal Crossing 49.91M / Super Smash Bros. Ultimate 37.76M cleanly). Audit-cycle-1 issued 6 required amendments + 12 per-question recommendations — all incorporated. Staged design is locked.
collection_summary.threshold_rule: Console partition: top 5 consoles by lifetime units sold per Wikipedia `List of best-selling game consoles` master ranking. Within-partition: top 3 titles per dedicated per-console best-seller list page (sorted by units sold DESC). Both rankings are source-defined; N=5 is the only curator-chosen cut.

N=5 yields a more deterministic cut. N=6 is still viable but the rank-6/rank-7 narrow gap makes the cutoff feel more arbitrary.

decision_log.decision: claim_type = source_defined (per audit-cycle-1 design review; deterministic-universe-rule preference satisfied)
decision_log.rationale: Single console-ranking master defines partition universe (top 5 by lifetime units sold); 5 dedicated per-console list pages supply ranked top-3 + value cells. Only curator input is N=5 (deterministic threshold on master ranking). No curator-rebuilt subset. Same pattern as zodiac-stars (source_count > 1 with each source carrying a single load-bearing role = source_defined claim_type).

Cycle-0 source exploration on 2026-05-18 found the universities candidate not viable for source-faithful staging — the WebFetch tool consistently truncated the universities master article before reaching the Latin America+Caribbean, North America, Oceania, and partial Asia sub-sections. Half the per-continent top-5 cells were unreachable from the live master. Pivot to video-games-per-platform preserves the hierarchical_decomposition saturator role (gap-1 → 5/5) with a source structure that uses bounded per-partition pages which the WebFetch tool can reliably fetch. The pivot decision itself is documented in the universities-instance comments.json trail.

decision_log.decision: N=5 (NOT N=6) for the top-consoles partition universe (per audit-cycle-1 amendment + per-question Q1)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1: N=5 yields 15 rows (clears ≥ 10 gate) and the boundary between rank-5 PS4 (117.2M) and rank-6 PS1 (102.49M) is wide (14.71M gap). N=6 yields 18 rows but the rank-6 vs rank-7 boundary is narrow (PS1 102.49M vs Wii 101.63M = 0.86M gap), making the cutoff feel more arbitrary. N=5 is the cleaner deterministic cut.

Per audit-cycle-1: the console master only defines the partition universe; each per-console list page supplies that partition's ranked row set + value cells. Each per-console page must be registered with roles like [universe, ranking, value]. Same pattern as zodiac-stars (source_count 13 with 1 Zodiac master + 12 per-constellation list pages). Per-console pages are NOT validation-only — they are universe+ranking+value-supplying for their partition.

decision_log.decision: Domain = Culture/Gaming (EXISTING subdomain, NOT new Technology/Gaming) per audit-cycle-1 amendment #1
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1: the repo already classifies the existing video-games instance (`trial_union_5`) under Culture/Gaming per `domain_taxonomy.md` and per-instance entity-class table. Cycle-0 design proposal incorrectly proposed Technology/Gaming as a NEW subdomain — would have invented a sibling subdomain for the same answer entity (video games). Reusing the existing Culture/Gaming subdomain is correct. Culture/Gaming extends from 1 to 2 instances; no NEW subdomain introduced.

decision_log.decision: Entity class = artifacts/video-games (EXISTING fine-class, NOT new) per audit-cycle-1 amendment + per-question Q11
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1: video games are artifacts per the existing taxonomy. The bucket `artifacts/*` is held by films + chemical-elements + songs + video-games + and just-extended buildings (skyscrapers). The `video-games` fine-class is held by `trial_union_5`. This instance is the 2nd video-games-keyed staged instance — NOT a NEW fine-class. Under answer-entity-wins, the composite PK (Console, Title) keys an individual video-game title, NOT the console — the Title is the answer entity, Console is the scaffold partition.

decision_log.decision: Schema = 4 cols (drop Publisher) per audit-cycle-1 amendment #3
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1: the PS2 and original PlayStation pages contain region-specific publisher cells in top rows (e.g., PS2 GTA: SA shows 'Rockstar Games (WW); Capcom (JP)'). Publisher as a scalar column would require multi-value normalization. Cleaner first-pass schema is 4 cols: Console + Title + Units Sold (millions) + Release Year. If a future-cycle audit prefers Publisher inclusion, the column would need to be staged as documented multi-value text.

Per audit-cycle-1 amendments #3 + #5: the Game Boy & Game Boy Color partition's top-3 includes grouped-generation entries (Pokémon Generation I = Red+Blue+Yellow; Pokémon Generation II = Gold+Silver+Crystal) which are not single-game rows. 'Titles' is honest about these grouped entries; 'video games' or 'games' would be less precise. ID + question wording + Title column header all use 'Title'.

decision_log.decision: Game Boy + Game Boy Color combined as single partition (per audit-cycle-1 per-question Q2)
decision_log.rationale: The master `List of best-selling game consoles` ranks Game Boy + Game Boy Color as a single combined platform entry (118.69M lifetime units sold). The dedicated best-seller list page also covers both as one combined ranking. Staged Console cell = 'Game Boy & Game Boy Color' verbatim from master. The top-3 entries include grouped-generation Pokémon titles per source convention.

decision_log.decision: Units Sold cells = numeric millions (NORMALIZED, not verbatim) per audit-cycle-1 per-question Q4
decision_log.rationale: Source uses heterogeneous formats: '71.08 million' (Switch table), '45,900,000' (Game Boy table comma-grouped integer), 'over 35 million copies of Tetris were shipped worldwide' (Game Boy Tetris row fuzzy text). Staged cells normalized to numeric millions with one-decimal precision: Switch MK8 → 71.08; Game Boy Pokémon Gen I → 45.90; Game Boy Tetris → 35.00 (lower bound of the 'over 35 million' phrasing, with fuzziness documented in normalization_decisions). Normalization is mechanical and source-traceable.

decision_log.decision: Year-anchor = artifact accessed 2026-05-18 + heterogeneous source-specific sales dating preserved
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 per-question Q5: each per-console list page carries its own sales-data dating (Switch as of March 31 2026; DS as of March 31 2025; Game Boy + Color last edited 2026-05-18 with per-row variation; PS2 + PS4 with per-row spread 2018-2023). Staging does NOT collapse these into a single global as-of (which would be factually wrong). The artifact-access date 2026-05-18 is the curator's snapshot; each partition's source-specific sales dating is preserved in source_coverage_notes::roles + temporal_note.

decision_log.decision: Sort = console-rank ASC (master partition order) primary; Units Sold DESC within partition; Release Year ASC tiebreak (not triggered)
decision_log.rationale: Primary partition order: PS2 (rank 1) → Switch (rank 2) → DS (rank 3) → Game Boy & Color (rank 4) → PS4 (rank 5) per the master ranking. Within each partition: source-ranked DESC by units sold. Tiebreak rule: Release Year ASC if two within-partition rows have identical Units Sold — not triggered at the staged 15-row universe (all within-partition values are distinct). Documented for future-cycle hygiene if a same-units-sold row enters a partition's top-3.

decision_log.decision: Release Year = integer extraction from full release date (NOT verbatim full date)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 per-question Q9: each per-console list has 'Release date' column with full date (e.g., 'October 26, 2004' for GTA: SA). Staged Release Year cells are integer-year extraction (2004), mirroring the asteroids' Discovery Year mechanical extraction precedent. Full release dates are documented in universe_listing notes but not staged in the CSV cell.

decision_log.decision: Operation type = projection (NOT topk) per audit-cycle-1 per-question Q10
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1: the artifact-contract canonical vocab does not include `topk` as an operation_type. Closest local precedent `top_5_highest_mountains_per_continent` uses `projection`. Same applied here.

decision_log.decision: PlayStation [PS1] master verbatim = 'PlayStation' (not staged; outside N=5 cut)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 per-question Q7: master labels the original PlayStation as 'PlayStation' (not 'PlayStation 1' or 'PS1'). PS1 ranks 6th at 102.49M lifetime — below the N=5 cut. Not in staged universe but the naming convention is documented for hygiene.

normalization_decisions.rule: Verbatim from master ranking. 5 values: 'PlayStation 2', 'Nintendo Switch', 'Nintendo DS', 'Game Boy & Game Boy Color', 'PlayStation 4'. The 'Game Boy & Game Boy Color' label uses the ampersand verbatim per master + per-partition list page — the combined-platform convention is source-defined.

Verbatim from per-console list page's title column. 15 unique values. Includes grouped-generation entries on the Game Boy & Game Boy Color partition ('Pokémon Generation I' combining Red + Blue + Yellow; 'Pokémon Generation II' combining Gold + Silver + Crystal) per the source's own row aggregation convention. Single-game entries elsewhere are verbatim master row labels (e.g., 'Marvel's Spider-Man' with apostrophe; 'New Super Mario Bros.' with terminal period; 'Super Smash Bros. Ultimate'). Diacritic preservation: 'Pokémon' (acute accent) preserved verbatim. The 'Nintendogs' row covers all four Nintendogs versions per master's single-row aggregation.

Numeric (float). Normalized to millions with up to two-decimal precision per master. Source forms heterogeneous: (a) '71.08 million' / '49.91 million' / etc. — Switch, PS2, PS4, DS pages — direct numeric extraction; (b) '45,900,000' / '30,000,000' / '35,000,000' — Game Boy page integers with commas (Pokémon Generation I, Pokémon Generation II, Tetris) — divided by 1,000,000 to convert to millions (45.90, 30.00, 35.00). Note on Tetris: the precise table-cell value is 35,000,000 (= 35.00 million staged); the article's separate INTRO PROSE uses the looser 'over 35 million' phrasing, but the staged cell is sourced from the precise table row, NOT the intro prose. Cycle-2 hygiene fix corrected an earlier conflation of the table-cell value with the intro's looser phrasing. Range: 14.2 (PS2 GTA: Vice City) to 71.08 (Switch Mario Kart 8 Deluxe).

Integer year (CE). Mechanical extraction of the calendar-year component from each per-console list page's 'Release date' or 'Release year' column. Range: 1989 (Game Boy Tetris) to 2020 (Switch Animal Crossing: New Horizons). For grouped-generation entries (Pokémon Generation I/II): Release Year = earliest sub-title release year (1996 for Gen I = Japanese Red/Green release; 1999 for Gen II = Japanese Gold/Silver release). Same mechanical-extraction precedent as asteroids' Discovery Year (extracted from master's full 'Date discovered' column).

open_questions.question: Should Publisher be added back as a documented multi-value text column in a future-cycle refinement?
open_questions.answer: Open for future-cycle consideration. Audit-cycle-1 dropped Publisher because PS2 + PS1 pages contain region-specific publisher cells (e.g., 'Rockstar Games (WW); Capcom (JP)' for GTA: SA). If a future audit wants Publisher inclusion, it would need to be staged as documented multi-value text with normalization rule (e.g., 'worldwide publisher only' or 'semicolon-delimited multi-region').

open_questions.question: If Nintendo Switch or PlayStation 4 sales figures shift over future seasons (Switch is still selling as of 2026), would the staged top-3 change?
open_questions.answer: Possibly. Within-partition top-3 is stable as of 2026-05-18 master access. The Switch top-3 (Mario Kart 8 Deluxe 71.08M / Animal Crossing 49.91M / Smash Ultimate 37.76M) has a wide gap from the 4th-rank (Zelda: BOTW ~32M), so the top-3 set is unlikely to shift in the near term. PS4 is end-of-life with stable figures. PS2 / DS / Game Boy & Color are commercially terminated platforms — staged values are stable in perpetuity.

open_questions.question: Should the staged universe expand to N=6 (add PS1 partition) if benchmark-coverage goals shift?
open_questions.answer: Open for future-cycle consideration. N=6 would add the PlayStation [PS1] partition with top-3 likely Gran Turismo 2 + Final Fantasy VII + Gran Turismo. The N=5 vs N=6 trade-off documented in alternative_partition_counts. Staying at N=5 keeps the cutoff at the wider PS4 vs PS1 boundary (117.2M-vs-102.49M).

open_questions.question: How should the staged design handle the Game Boy Tetris 'over 35 million' fuzziness if a future-cycle audit objects to the 35.00 lower-bound staging?
open_questions.answer: Alternative options: (a) stage as null with a 'fuzzy figure' note; (b) stage as a range '35-40' as text; (c) stage as 35.00 with the fuzziness documented (current choice). The current choice mirrors the asteroid ± uncertainty band stripping precedent (central value used; uncertainty documented). If audit prefers a different approach, the cell can be updated; the master value's fuzziness is the source's own framing.

cycle_1_audit_design_review.verdict: APPROVE WITH AMENDMENTS (6 required amendments + 12 per-question recommendations)
amendments: 1. Change domain to Culture/Gaming (NOT Technology/Gaming). The repo already classifies the existing video-games instance under Culture/Gaming per domain_taxonomy.md:38 and instance_selection_priorities.md:1750; reuse existing subdomain rather than inventing a sibling for the same answer entity.

2. Set source_count = 6 for the N=5 version and register every per-console list page. The console master only defines the partition universe; each per-console page supplies its partition's ranked row set + values, so each must be registered with [universe, ranking, value] roles — same pattern as zodiac-stars.
